dirty_scope: GSQ/RCO architecture plan and preflight files from this task plus the new trace-derived REAP control tool, tests, quality-gate wiring, receipt, and architecture update.
scope: Implement the deterministic REAP-style control arm for Qwen expert pruning from real --dump-routing traces. The tool parses the engine trace format, scores experts by router weight or activation count, keeps an exact per-layer budget, emits a hash-bound JSON mask and optional Strata profile, and reports trace coverage. It prepares for real trace capture; no real trace existed in this checkout and no pruning/model run ran.

trace_contract.record: int32 layer, int32 k, k int32 expert ids, k float32 router weights
trace_contract.serve_mode: drive_pool_multi emits unit-frequency records with zero float weights; weighted mode therefore treats zero weights as one activation

selection_contract: Primary key: descending weighted score, or descending activation count with --unweighted
Tie key: ascending original expert id
Sparse layers are filled by ascending expert id and fill IDs are reported separately
Output mask records every input path and SHA-256
Optional profile is written through tools/make_profile.py and read back in tests

checks.result: 5 tests passed: weighted deterministic selection, zero-weight serve records, exact sparse fills, CLI/profile round trip, truncated trace rejection
all checks passed even though tools/ is excluded from the maintained-scripts gate

quality_wiring: scripts/strata.py now runs python3 -m unittest tools.test_reap_mask_from_traces as the compression-tools domain in just quality.
non_claims: No routing trace file existed in this checkout, so no real mask was generated here.
No model was loaded and no RCO/GSQ/LoRA/pruning/quantization/inference ran.
This is a heuristic REAP-style control, not RCO's joint full-model KL optimization.
Router-weight ranking may not equal output-quality preservation; the generated mask must compete against RCO on the same held-out acceptance set.
No claim is made that 256 experts per layer is optimal for our workload.
